Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law

defence noun

in a court of law

also defense, the defence, speak in one’s defence, plead one’s case, defend (in court), case for the defence

classical

Cic. Cael. 4: ad istam omnem ōrātiōnem brevis est dēfēnsiō (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Mil. 15

dēfēnsiō, dēfēnsiōnis f.

noun, third declension · Declension on Wiktionary

a defence; the speech or case for the accused

Also any defending: of a town (Caes. B.G. 2.7), of a friend’s standing (Cic. Fam. 1.7.2).

Other words

  • causam dīcere — to answer a charge, make one’s defence

    phrase: causa, causae f. with dīcō, dīcere, dīxī, dictum · also used · classical · Cic. Rosc. Am. 12 (Lewis & Short); Liv. 29.19.5

    Said of the accused defending himself, and of the advocate pleading for him (Lewis & Short).

  • dēfendō, dēfendere, dēfendī, dēfēnsum — to defend (someone in court)

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Phil. 2.8: inter sīcāriōs dēfendere (Lewis & Short, s.v. sīcārius); Traupman 194: causam alicūjus dēfendere, defend someone · Conjugation on Wiktionary

    The general verb for defending and protecting (see protect). In court, of the advocate: inter sīcāriōs dēfendere, to defend on a charge of murder.

Examples

  • ad istam omnem ōrātiōnem brevis est dēfēnsiō.

    to all that speech of yours the defence is short.Cic. Cael. 4 (Lewis & Short)

See also lawyer, trial, case, court, protect.
